survey.scope: All Atrinik organization consumers and producers of legacy map, nested-object, archetype, artifact, treasure, region, faction, and interface syntax
survey.method: Reviewed server Flex and C entry points plus Python, PHP, Java-lineage, and collection code in the content and tools repositories

consumers.behavior: Stages tracked tools and authored sources, invokes collection in isolation, and emits a digest manifest.
consumers.parity_requirement: A replacement must preserve source immutability, attribution, atomic publication, and deterministic runtime bytes.

consumers.behavior: Reads significant lines and XML into typed stable definitions, references, and deterministic diagnostics; it intentionally does not preserve representation.
consumers.parity_requirement: The lossless core must reproduce catalog definitions, references, source locations, and errors before this partial parser is removed.

consumers.behavior: Parses ADS-1 XML interfaces and writes generated embedded Python and the quest registry.
consumers.parity_requirement: Schema validation, XML source locations, quest-part UIDs, and generated behavior must remain equivalent.

consumers.behavior: Concatenates nested authored definitions into top-level runtime aggregates and invokes the interface compiler.
consumers.parity_requirement: Ordering, comments required by runtime readers, generated aggregate bytes, and source-clean operation require golden comparisons.

consumers.behavior: Uses multiple simple line parsers for exploratory deterministic reports and strips multiline-message representation.
consumers.parity_requirement: Every reported quest, region, artifact, map, object, and source location must be reproduced before consolidating it.

consumers.behavior: Loads collected Object records and More multipart continuations in MAP_STYLE line mode through the case-insensitive Flex object grammar.
consumers.parity_requirement: Object defaults, multipart linkage, custom fields, stable IDs, messages, case folding, and LL_MORE/LL_NORMAL/LL_ERROR outcomes are authoritative.

consumers.behavior: Parses artifact headers in C, then delegates Object bodies to the Flex loader in MAP_ARTIFACT mode.
consumers.parity_requirement: Allowed masks, chance fields, copy behavior, embedded object text, and error boundaries must match.

consumers.behavior: Requires the exact LF arch-map sentinel, parses a case-insensitive header, then recursively loads object inventories with MAP_ORIGINAL side effects.
consumers.parity_requirement: Header defaults and flags, tiling, object stacks, inventory depth, exit fields, custom fields, and loader return codes are authoritative.

consumers.behavior: Writes normalized LF map headers and object differences; it does not preserve comments, field order, whitespace, or original line endings.
consumers.parity_requirement: Runtime save/reload semantics must compare equal even though authored no-op editing must use the later lossless writer.

consumers.behavior: The common case-insensitive Flex grammar supports file, buffer, NUL-string, and single-variable modes, raw messages, and arbitrary key/value extensions; only FILE line mode has the ten-entry object stack bound.
consumers.parity_requirement: All known fields, unknown fields, identity validation, nesting, messages, line endings, and mode-specific return codes require differential tests.

consumers.behavior: Serializes differences from an archetype in a fixed normalized field order and writes custom key/value extensions first.
consumers.parity_requirement: Every persisted field and recursive inventory must survive load-save-load semantic comparison.

consumers.behavior: Uses the common object grammar for durable player objects and inventories, adding migration-sensitive stable spell and skill IDs.
consumers.parity_requirement: Existing durable saves must load identically and repeated migration/save cycles must be stable.

consumers.behavior: Uses a bespoke line reader with msg/endmsg, parent links, jail coordinates, and strict block endings.
consumers.parity_requirement: Region hierarchy, inherited text/map metadata, message bytes, and malformed-block errors must match.

consumers.behavior: Uses a recursive bespoke line parser for treasure, treasureone, list links, item attributes, and yes/no branching.
consumers.parity_requirement: Entry order, probabilities, recursion, list references, attributes, and malformed-input diagnostics must match.

consumers.behavior: Uses exact LF and case-sensitive line parsing, recursively materializes inventories, and emits severity-ranked gameplay/content diagnostics.
consumers.parity_requirement: The corpus freezes accepted/rejected boundaries and diagnostic meaning before this duplicate parser is retired.

consumers.behavior: The historical Java editor source is external and only a build/download wrapper remains in the content repository.
consumers.parity_requirement: Representative Gridarta-produced maps are corpus inputs; no unreviewed external parser may define the new syntax.

consumers.behavior: Provides a second recursive parser/object model and a normalizing map saver for checker auto-fixes and the interface editor.
consumers.parity_requirement: Inventory structure, attributes, diagnostics, and intended auto-fixes must be represented as shared inspection and byte-patch contracts.

consumers.behavior: Copies an existing maps tree and other release inputs byte-for-byte into the historical map-maker package; it does not parse or generate ADS records.
consumers.parity_requirement: Collection must not rewrite authored content, and any revived packager must consume the shared runtime collection boundary instead of acquiring a parser.

consumers.behavior: Writes map grids and rewrites tile_path fields with exact LF byte assumptions and whole-file truncation.
consumers.parity_requirement: Tiling topology must compare semantically and any future patch must be conflict-detecting and preserve unrelated bytes.

consumers.behavior: A copied exploratory analyzer duplicates the content-owned tool and its partial line parsers.
consumers.parity_requirement: Remove this copy after the content-owned analyzer and shared contracts cover every report consumer.

consumers.behavior: Uses PHP sscanf and exact-line loops to load collected archetypes and maps for a web renderer, ignoring many fields and representation details.
consumers.parity_requirement: Rendered object placement, multipart geometry, faces, animations, and artifact overlays need scene-level comparison before removal.

reviewed_non_consumers.reason: Consumes streamed protocol state and collected graphics, not authored ADS files.
The standalone repository is currently an empty native-editor shell; the historical Gridarta wrapper remains under atrinik/content/editor.
Owns wire contracts only and has no authored-content file parser.
